correctness.rationale: Verified the actual pinned RESULT.md proof and immutable Git tree 5149c51e0f88940e9020d427dfe02fee90ed11cb. Ardila--Escobar Proposition 3.8 has exactly the two affine sums C_n=n(n+1)/2+1 and 3^n-3 minimal bisubset facets. Projecting x_i=1 and y_i=1 normals onto the codimension-two affine tangent space gives length sqrt((n-1)/n); summing the shifted coordinate-facet inequalities yields r<=(mu_n-1)/sqrt((n-1)/n) and forces the unique uniform center at equality for n>=3. For any bisubset, with w=|S cap T| and d=|S\T|-|T\S|, the independently derived Q=n^2-w^2-d^2 satisfies projected norm^2=Q/(2n), uniform-center slack=Q/4+w/n and distance sqrt(nQ/8)+w sqrt(2/(nQ)). For w>=1, Q>=2w(n-w)>=2(n-1)>4w/n; the distance increases with Q and w so its unique equality class is w=1,Q=2(n-1), exactly 2n coordinate facets. For w=0, Q>=4(n-1), giving strictly larger distance for n>=3. At n=2 six facet distances have a diagonal pair summing to 2; radius 1 forces p=q and coordinate distances give |p|<=1-1/sqrt(2). Independently checked both symbolic identities with SymPy; enumerated all bisubsets (3^n-3) for n=2..8 using exact fractions, confirming formula and active counts; solved the independent Chebyshev linear program for n=2..5 with expected optima. These tests corroborate, not substitute for, the arbitrary-n proof.

value.rationale: The harmonic polytope is a standard, independently motivated Minkowski-sum model arising in matroid conormal geometry. Its largest intrinsic Euclidean ball is a natural exact metric invariant not recovered from known face and volume formulas or from its vertex-shell circumradius. The final theorem provides an all-rank closed form, uniqueness for n>=3, an unexpectedly small 2n-contact subset of 3^n-3 facets and the rank-two positive-dimensional center locus. The global slack minimization and sharp boundary behavior are mathematical structural facts plausibly useful to geometric researchers, not a textbook relabeling or unmotivated finite sample.

final_claim: For the standard Ardila--Escobar harmonic polytope H_{n,n} in its inherited Euclidean affine metric, every n>=3 has unique incenter ((n+1)/2+1/n)(1_n,1_n) and inradius (n^2-n+2)/(2 sqrt(n(n-1))), with only the 2n coordinate facets tangent; n=2 has radius 1 and all centers ((2+t,2-t),(2+t,2-t)) for |t|<=1-1/sqrt(2). No affine-invariant or John-ellipsoid claim.
limitations: Scientific finding is for the fixed inherited Euclidean metric and n>=2 only; no claim about n=1, John ellipsoid, circumradius or affine invariance.
Finite enumeration and linear programs only corroborate the symbolic argument, not a general-rank proof by themselves.
Originality remains best-of-knowledge with documented unindexed Chebyshev-center and folklore risks, not independent global priority certification.
